Q: React Native can't correctly display number A:

Fix for React Native Android: Two-digit numbers cut off in small circle

Problem
On Android, numbers like 18, 19, 21 appear cut off, shifted down, or misaligned inside small fixed-size circles (e.g. 28×28 px), while single digits (like 2) look fine.

Root Cause
Android Text component has inconsistent vertical padding + font metrics issues when centering text in small containers.

Recommended Solution (works best in 2025–2026)

Update your styles:

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  circle: {
    width: 32,                    // safer than 28
    height: 32,
    borderRadius: 16,
    backgroundColor: '#2196F3',
    justifyContent: 'center',
    alignItems: 'center',
    marginRight: 12,
  },

  circleText: {
    color: '#fff',
    fontSize: 15,                 // 14–16 is sweet spot
    fontWeight: '600',            // or 'bold'
    lineHeight: 32,               // ← most important fix
    textAlign: 'center',
    includeFontPadding: false,    // ← removes extra Android padding
  },
});

Q: How to use mage.exe for (re)signing manifests with Azure Trusted Code Signing A:

From https://solutionfall.com/question/can-azure-trusted-signing-be-used-to-sign-manifest-files-with-or-without-mageexe/ i get:

"Azure Trusted Signing cannot be used to sign Manifest files directly, whether with or without Mage.exe. Azure Trusted Signing is designed specifically for signing software artifacts such as executables, libraries, and container images stored in Azure services. It provides an extra layer of security and trust by verifying the authenticity and integrity of the signed artifacts. Manifest files, on the other hand, are typically used for ClickOnce deployments and do not fall under the scope of Azure Trusted Signing. If you need to sign Manifest files, you should use tools like Mage.exe or SignTool.exe, which are specifically designed for signing ClickOnce manifests."

I research the way with a Zertifcate stored in Azure-KeyVault. In https://github.com/dotnet/sign you can read supported FileTypes: ClickOnce .application and .vsto (via Mage).

But the referenced notes missing the point with mage.

  • ClickOnce/VSTO manifest signing (.application, .vsto, .manifest) still relies on Mage, and Mage cannot use Azure Key Vault remote signing today. (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1337830/how-to-interact-with-azure-key-vault-to-sign-the-c)

  • Even Azure Trusted Signing currently doesn’t support ClickOnce application/manifest files.
    (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1791756/how-to-sign-clickonce-application-manifest-file-wi)

    So currently i check out https://www.davici.nl/clickonce-signing-from-azure-devops-via-azure-key-vault/ to sign my office addin.

    davici’s tool is not “calling mage.exe with a Key Vault cert” (that still wouldn’t work). Instead, it:

    1. Uses AzureSignTool for PE files (.exe/.dll) via Key Vault (remote signing / HSM-backed key).

    2. For ClickOnce/VSTO manifests, it doesn’t use the stock Mage toolchain as-is. It bundles Mage’s signing logic (“mage code”) into the tool and plugs in a signer that can perform the RSA signing operation via Key Vault (so it doesn’t require an exportable private key on disk / in the cert store). That’s exactly what the davici post + repo describe (“combined AzureSignTool with the source code of mage.exe”).

    So: Mage.exe can’t sign with Key Vault, but a Mage-like implementation can, if you replace “local private key” with “remote sign() via Key Vault”.
